origin.note: ECC is used as a source of patterns and as the benchmark to beat; every adopted skill keeps its id and origin.

categories.name: Engineering
categories.description: How code is written, tested, reviewed and verified here. Every other category assumes these rules hold.
categories.gate: No change is finished without tdd-workflow and verification-loop evidence.
rules: Write the failing test before the implementation.
Never call a task done without real execution evidence (test, build, lint).
One skill is one procedure with a machine-checkable exit.
Skill ids are stable; renaming breaks the registry, routing and journals.

skills.description: Red-green-refactor with a coverage gate so a task is never called done on inspection alone.
Six-phase verification (build, types, lint, tests+coverage, security, diff review) with quotable evidence for each.
Baseline conventions for naming, size, immutability and error visibility so review discusses behaviour, not style.
Fresh-context diff review: real defects ranked by severity, with a verdict at the end.
Search the repo, npm and PyPI before writing a dependency, helper or module.
Incremental build, type and lint repair: one error per cycle, root cause before patch.
Verified removal of dead code and duplicate logic, one candidate per commit, suite green throughout.
Turn 'it is slow' into a measured change: baseline, one bottleneck, one hypothesis, compare.
End-to-end flows with page objects, stable locators and quarantine for flaky tests.
Turn every fixed defect into a permanent regression test that runs without external services.
Make failures loud, typed and recoverable instead of swallowed or converted to null.
One taxonomy, one policy: every failure carries a stable code, severity, owner and retry rule.

categories.name: Contracts
categories.description: Machine-checkable promises between skills, modules and services: schemas, versions and breaking-change rules.
categories.gate: A contract version is immutable; a breaking change needs a new major file and a migration note.
rules: Contracts are schemas plus a version plus consumers, never prose.
Adding optional fields is minor; removing fields or adding required ones is major.
Consumers pin a major version and accept any same-major producer.
Validation runs before the payload is used, not after it fails.

skills.description: Design a contract from the consumers' needs: minimal fields, explicit required set, versioned from day one.
Validate payloads against their contract before use, with deterministic first-error reporting.
Evolve a schema without breaking consumers: classify every change and require the right version bump.
Check a consumer against a producer across majors and report what breaks and where.

categories.name: Protocols
categories.description: Typed, versioned hand-offs between roles. A malformed message is rejected, never repaired.
categories.gate: Zero malformed messages accepted: parse, validate, then process, in that order.
rules: Every message carries an envelope: protocol, version, task, origin, target, id.
A receiver refuses versions it does not declare.
Unknown fields are errors, not noise: they hide producer bugs.
Evidence without a source is not evidence.

skills.description: Design a message protocol: envelope, payload, consumers, versioning and rejection rules.
Validate a stream or file of protocol messages and report the first rejection with its code.
Derive and maintain a message schema from a dataclass so code and contract cannot drift.

categories.name: Error administration
categories.description: The lifecycle of failure: taxonomy, recovery contract, forensics and retry policy.
categories.gate: No error reaches a boundary without a code, an owner and a recovery contract.
rules: Every error has a stable code; the code is what callers branch on.
An error says what to do next or it is not finished.
Retries are policy, not reflex: only retryable codes, with a stop condition.
The journal is the source of truth for what happened; the console is a summary.

skills.description: Attach a recovery contract to every error path: root-cause hint, safe retry, stop condition.
Reconstruct a run from its journal: what ran, what failed, what was retried, and where the chain broke.
Decide retryability per error code, with backoff, budget and a stop condition that cannot loop forever.
Turn recurring failures into tracked, deduplicated work items with evidence and owners.

categories.name: Agentic
categories.description: Design, measure and audit agents: action space, evals, context budget and loop safety.
categories.gate: No change to an agent is accepted without an eval before and after.
rules: Define what 'task completed' means before designing tools or prompts.
Long guidance lives in skills loaded on demand, never in the system prompt.
Diagnose by layer with the trace in hand; rewriting the prompt is the last resort.
A loop without a stop condition is an outage waiting for a clock.

skills.description: Design action space, tool granularity, observation format and context budget for higher completion rates.
Eval-driven development: criteria before the change, cheapest grader that works, pass@k and pass^k.
Layer-by-layer diagnosis of an agent stack with severity-ranked findings and concrete patches.
Spend context deliberately: measure what is loaded, cap it, and compact at phase boundaries.
Run unattended loops safely: explicit stop conditions, budgets, checkpoints and human gates.

categories.name: Security
categories.description: Secrets, dependencies, destructive operations and adversarial review of agent output.
categories.gate: Security findings of high severity block the run; they are not advisory.
rules: Read-only first: audit before proposing changes.
A secret found in the repo is rotated, not just deleted.
Destructive operations need explicit consent, never a default.
Scanning your own configuration is part of the job, not an extra.

skills.description: Adversarial review of a diff for reachable vulnerabilities, ranked by exploitability.
Find credentials and high-entropy strings in the tree and diff, with rotation guidance.
Guard destructive operations behind risk levels and explicit confirmation.
Audit imports and dependencies for unused, unpinned or unreviewed packages.

categories.name: Data and persistence
categories.description: Schemas that outlive code: migrations, query review and caching decisions.
categories.gate: A migration without a tested reverse path does not ship.
rules: Data outlives code: version the storage, not just the API.
Every migration states its rollback and its data-loss window.
A cache is a correctness decision disguised as a performance one.
Queries are reviewed with the plan, not the query text alone.

skills.description: Define the shape and invariants of persisted data before the code that touches it.
Write reversible migrations with backfill plans, lock analysis and a tested rollback.
Review queries with their access plan: N+1, missing indexes, unbounded scans.
Decide what to cache, for how long, and how to invalidate, before adding a cache.

categories.name: Reverse engineering
categories.description: Understand and reconstruct systems from artefacts: binaries, traffic, undocumented APIs.
categories.gate: Every finding is tied to an artefact (offset, string, packet) or it is a guess.
rules: Evidence first: artefact, offset, hash. A hypothesis without an artefact is a guess.
Never execute an unknown sample outside an isolated environment.
Reconstruction is validated by replaying real observed traffic.
Document the protocol with the same rigour as production code.

skills.description: Recover the behaviour of an unknown system: static triage, dynamic observation, protocol reconstruction, report.
First pass on an unknown binary: type, architecture, strings, imports, packing signals, without executing it.
Rebuild an undocumented HTTP API from captured traffic into an openapi-style spec and a validated client.

categories.name: Governance
categories.description: The package administers itself: registration, audit of existing skills, versioning and changelog discipline.
categories.gate: Nothing enters the package without passing `workflow validate --strict` and a registration record.
rules: The registry is the source of truth: on-disk without registered is an error.
New skills are scaffolded by `workflow new`, never hand-built.
Every edit bumps metadata.version and lands a CHANGELOG line.
A skill that cannot state its exit criteria is a note, not a skill.

skills.description: Register and author a new skill end to end: decision tests, scaffolding, manifest, validation, changelog.
Audit the catalogue for overlap, dead skills, weak triggers and skills that never fire.
Keep a changelog that a consumer can act on: what changed, what breaks, what to do.

categories.name: Product and UX
categories.description: User-facing quality: accessibility, flows and interface craft.
categories.gate: Accessibility findings of level AA failures block, level AAA advise.
rules: Accessibility is a correctness requirement, not a polish item.
A flow is audited by clicking it, not by reading it.
Every interface change states what it makes possible.

skills.description: Audit a UI against WCAG 2.2 AA: contrast, focus order, targets, semantics, keyboard paths.

categories.name: Content and docs
categories.description: Written artefacts that ship with the code: documentation and changelogs.
categories.gate: nothing published without an executed example, a named source of truth and a last-verified date
rules: Docs that drift are worse than no docs: every doc names its source of truth.
Write for the reader who has to act, not for the reader who has to admire.

skills.description: Write and review documentation that stays true: source of truth, audience, failure modes, examples that run.
